title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC Seth-act precedes imputation tip
pass_a_gloss: The act that first made us human is Adam's begetting of Seth; so antecedent/immediate first-sin imputation presupposes it. We count as Adam's offspring before we count as sinners; we are posterity because he begot us, and he begot us as he begot Seth. Seth's begetting precedes sin-imputation in nature's order. Yet on the Learned Man's view the sin was charged at the moment of commission—long before Seth—so either imputation also ran ahead of Adam's own coming-to-be. Tip closes Q5.
pass_b_english: But that act by which we were first made humans is that act of generating by which Adam begot Seth: therefore the antecedent or immediate imputation of the first sin presupposes that act. Earlier, then, was it that we be counted as begotten from Adam than as sinners, and that first act by which we were begotten belonged to us earlier than that by which we were made sinners. For Adam's sin is imputed to us because we are his posterity; and we are his posterity because he begot us; and he begot us insofar as he begot Seth. Therefore the act by which he begot Seth precedes the imputation of sin in the order of nature. And yet, if the learned man is believed, Adam's sin was imputed to us long before he had begotten Seth, at the very time it was committed: either then it also preceded Adam's coming to be.
source_text: Is autem actus, quo primo facti sumus homines, est actus ille generandi, quo Adamus Sethum genuit: quare imputatio peccati primi antecedens seu immediata supponit illum actum. Prius igitur fuit nos haberi pro genitis ab Adamo, quam pro peccatoribus, & primus ille actus quo geniti sumus prius ad nos pertinuit, quam ille quo facti sumus peccatores. Imputatur enim nobis peccatum Adae, quia sumus eius posteri: sumus autem eius posteri, quia nos genuit: nos autem genuit, quatenus genuit Sethum. Actus ergo quo genuit Sethum ordine naturae antecedit imputationem peccati. Sed tamen, si viro docto fides habetur, imputatum est nobis peccatum Adami diu antequam Sethum genuisset, illo ipso tempore quo commissum est: aut igitur antecessit etiam fieri Adami.
